column1: # Section-level exclusions for the normative-requirement coverage audit.
# specs/audit-scope.tsv decides whether a specification imposes obligations at
# all. This file is finer grained: it drops individual sections of an in-scope
# specification whose requirements are addressed to an actor Vouch is not, or
# cover a feature Vouch does not implement by design.
# An excluded statement is not "untested" -- it is not owed. It never enters the
# in-scope denominator and never lands in specs/coverage-baseline.tsv, so the
# backlog stays a list of real work.
# section_prefix matches a section and everything beneath it: "4" excludes 4,
# 4.8 and 4.8.1, but not 40. The reason column is required and must say what
# makes the section inapplicable, with the evidence -- the next person to read
# it needs to be able to check the claim, not just take it.
# crates/vouch-tests/tests/spec_coverage.rs enforces two rules that keep this
#   1. An exclusion matching no statement fails the build. Sections get
#      renumbered when a spec is re-cached, and a stale exclusion would
#   2. An excluded section that a test cites fails the build. The exclusion
#      claims Vouch has no obligation there while a test asserts behavior, so
#      one of the two is wrong and a human has to say which.

column3: Section 5 is "User Agent Requirements" -- the browser-side cookie storage and parsing algorithm. Vouch is a server (Section 4); the CLI writes a Netscape cookie file for curl interop and implements no part of the UA algorithm.
JWS JSON Serialization. Vouch uses compact serialization throughout; no code path produces or parses the general or flattened JSON forms.

TLS requirements for retrieving key material named by the "jku" and "x5u" header parameters. The section is scoped by its opening sentence, "Implementations supporting the \"jku\" and/or \"x5u\" Header Parameters MUST support TLS"; Vouch supports neither, dereferences no header-supplied URL (grep for jku/x5u across crates/*/src returns nothing), and pins that refusal in test_rfc7515_header_supplied_key_material_is_not_a_key_source.

JWE key management algorithms (RSAES, ECDH-ES, AES-KW, PBES2). Vouch implements no JWE: services/oidc/jar.rs rejects five-part tokens, and the only algorithms produced or verified anywhere are ES256, RS256, PS256, EdDSA and HS256.
JWE content encryption algorithms (AES-CBC-HMAC, AES-GCM). Same reason as section 4 -- no JWE support.
Refresh token guidance. Vouch issues no refresh tokens by design; see the section 4.14 row.

Refresh token replay detection, rotation and binding. Vouch issues no refresh tokens by design -- services/oidc/grant_type.rs has no refresh grant, and services/oidc/registration.rs treats refresh_token as registration-only ("accepted in registration, though never issued"). The underlying threat is answered by short-lived DPoP-bound access tokens with no long-lived credential to replay.

Attacks on in-browser communication flows -- authorization responses delivered by postMessage instead of HTTP redirects. Not implemented: no occurrence of postMessage or web_message in the workspace, ResponseMode has no such variant, and response_modes_supported advertises only query, form_post and the JARM forms. Pinned by test_rfc9700_authorization_response_is_never_delivered_in_browser, which cites the conditional requirement in section 2.6 rather than this section.
CredentialRequestOptions dictionary extension -- addressed to the client, not the Relying Party.
The authenticatorMakeCredential operation -- addressed to the authenticator, not the Relying Party.
The authenticatorGetAssertion operation -- addressed to the authenticator, not the Relying Party. Its Relying Party counterpart is section 7.2, which is in scope.

String truncation of authenticator-stored strings. Every statement is addressed to the authenticator or, where it compensates for one, to the user agent: "Conforming User Agents are responsible for ensuring that the authenticator behaviour observed by Relying Parties conforms to this specification with respect to string handling." Vouch is neither.

The optional language and base-direction suffix a string may carry -- "To encode language and direction metadata in a string that is documented as permitting it, suffix its code points with two sequences of code points". Vouch encodes no such suffix on any name it sends, so the one recommendation in the section (use a directionality marker only when needed) has nothing to apply to.

The template a specification must follow when it defines a new attestation statement format -- "Each attestation statement format MUST be defined using the following template". Addressed to whoever defines a format, not to a Relying Party verifying one. The formats Vouch verifies are section 8.2 (packed) and its certificate requirements in 8.2.1, both in scope.

Generating an attestation object -- "the authenticator MUST" perform the listed steps. Addressed to the authenticator. The signature encodings a verifier depends on are section 6.5.5, which is in scope and cited by crypto/webauthn_verify.rs.

TPM attestation statement certificate requirements. Vouch never verifies a tpm attestation statement: attestation.rs classifies the format as a platform authenticator and validate_hardware_attestation refuses the registration before any certificate is parsed. Pinned by test_format_classification.
Android Key attestation statement format. Rejected for the same reason as the tpm format above -- android-key is classified as a platform authenticator, so no Android key attestation is ever parsed.
